name: Zinc
description: Iran’s zinc industry connects mineral extraction with metal production and applications such as corrosion protection and brassmaking. Understanding it requires distinguishing the weight of concentrate from its contained zinc and from finished metal.

seo.title: Zinc in Iran: Deposits, Production and Industrial Uses
seo.description: Explore Iran’s zinc deposits, the distinction between concentrate and metal, and the evidence available for annual production.

content.heading: A metal that protects other metals
content.content:
Zinc’s industrial importance extends beyond objects made primarily from zinc. Galvanizing uses zinc as a protective coating on iron and steel, linking the metal to the durability of manufactured products and infrastructure. Other applications include brass, zinc-based die-casting alloys and rolled zinc. Zinc compounds also serve rubber, chemical, paint and agricultural industries. These are global applications; the inspected evidence does not establish their respective shares of Iranian consumption. [s2]

Sphalerite, a zinc sulfide, is the principal zinc ore mineral worldwide. However, an account of Iran’s deposits must also recognize carbonate mineralization rather than assuming that all zinc ore has the same composition or geological history. [s2][s3]

content.heading: Contrasting deposits
content.content:
Angouran in northwestern Iran illustrates this mineralogical variety. A published study describes successive sulfide and carbonate stages of mineralization, including sphalerite and smithsonite, a zinc carbonate. Its abstract supports that geological distinction, but historical grades reported there should not be treated as current operating grades or remaining reserves. [s3]

Mehdiabad, in the southern Yazd Basin of central Iran, provides a different geological setting. A research abstract describes zinc-lead mineralization hosted in shale, siltstone and dolomite within the Taft Formation. The authors interpret it as a sedimentary-exhalative system involving replacement beneath the ancient seafloor. This is a geological interpretation; it does not establish the present operating status of a mine or processing project. [s4]

content.heading: Reading the production evidence
content.content:
The USGS distinguishes zinc contained in mine concentrates from zinc metal produced at the smelting stage. The chart follows contained zinc, avoiding the misleading comparison of concentrate weight with finished metal. Most values in the inspected zinc production rows are estimates, so repeated figures should not be read as proof of precisely unchanged operations. [s1]

A fuller assessment still needs verified plant-level output, feedstock movements and environmental monitoring. Mineral resources, installed processing capacity and actual annual production answer different questions and should remain separate.

name: Industrial Alloys
description: Industrial alloys connect Iran’s metal supply with materials designed for machining, wear resistance, heat and corrosion. Producer documentation shows a varied steel product portfolio, while national ferrochromium statistics describe only one upstream input.

seo.title: Industrial Alloys in Iran: Inputs, Steel Grades and Processing
seo.description: Understand Iran’s alloy-steel product families, the role of ferrochromium, and the limits of national production statistics.

content.heading: Materials distinguished by their intended work
content.content:
An industrial alloy is useful because of the properties it delivers in service. Chromium illustrates the connection: it contributes corrosion and oxidation resistance, wear resistance and strength at elevated temperatures. Ferrochromium, an iron-chromium alloy, is an important additive for stainless-steel production. Chromite ore, ferrochromium and finished stainless steel are therefore distinct stages and products. [s2]

This distinction matters when reading Iranian industry statistics. A ferroalloy production figure measures an input to downstream manufacturing; it cannot establish how much finished alloy steel was made or which grades reached customers.

content.heading: What Iranian producer documentation shows
content.content:
Iran Alloy Steel Company’s product classification includes heat-treatable, heat-resistant, tool, free-cutting, stainless and case-hardening steels, alongside spring, bearing, valve and plastic-mould steels. These categories organize materials around different manufacturing and service requirements. [s3]

The distinctions are practical. Tool steels serve tools and dies; free-cutting steels emphasize machinability. Case-hardening steels are intended for components requiring a hard, wear-resistant surface, while heat-resistant steels address elevated-temperature service. The company’s classification establishes its advertised portfolio, rather than independently verified shipment volumes or performance for every grade. [s3]

Its homepage also describes steelmaking, light and heavy rolling, heat treatment, finishing and inspection. The central laboratory is presented as performing chemical, physical and mechanical tests. Together, these descriptions show that alloy production involves processing and verification as well as composition. They do not independently establish certification scope or customer acceptance. [s4]

content.heading: A narrow statistical window
content.content:
The accompanying series covers ferrochromium alone. It should not be labeled total Iranian alloy output. A national picture would additionally require comparable production and trade evidence for other alloying inputs and finished grades. [s1]

The useful conclusion is that Iran’s alloy sector should be understood through both material specifications and the stages of manufacture. Tonnage is informative only when its product boundary is explicit.

name: Specialty Metals
description: Specialty metals contribute particular properties to alloys and other industrial materials. Molybdenum provides a documented Iranian production example, although mine concentrate statistics do not establish domestic production of every downstream specialty product.

seo.title: Specialty Metals in Iran: Molybdenum and the Evidence Boundary
seo.description: Explore molybdenum’s industrial role and Iranian production evidence, with clear distinctions between concentrate, contained metal and finished products.

content.heading: A category defined by function
content.content:
For this guide, specialty metals are considered through the particular properties they bring to industrial materials. Molybdenum is an instructive example: its most common use is as an alloying agent in stainless steels, alloy steels and superalloys, improving hardness, strength and corrosion resistance. Its industrial significance therefore cannot be judged by tonnage alone. [s2]

Molybdenite is the principal mineral source of molybdenum. Recognizing the distinction between a mineral feedstock and an alloying material helps explain why evidence of mining does not by itself demonstrate a complete domestic manufacturing chain. [s2]

content.heading: What the Iranian evidence establishes
content.content:
USGS reports Iranian molybdenum mine output in both concentrate weight and contained molybdenum. The series below uses contained metal, allowing comparison without treating changing concentrate composition as an equivalent change in metal output. It documents an upstream activity; it does not measure production of purified metal, alloy additions or finished components. [s1]

Chromium offers a related materials example. It contributes corrosion and oxidation resistance and is used in stainless steels and superalloys. However, evidence concerning chromium-bearing materials must identify whether it concerns ore, ferrochromium or chromium metal. Those forms have different processing requirements and industrial roles. [s3]

content.heading: From mineral availability to demonstrated capability
content.content:
The central editorial question is how far a documented supply chain extends. A useful industry account would connect extraction with recovery, refining, product specification and verified industrial use. This draft establishes a molybdenum production series and explains relevant material functions, but it does not establish that entire chain in Iran.

Claims about titanium, rare-earth metals, high-purity products or advanced specialty components require their own inspected evidence. They are excluded here pending research rather than inferred from geological occurrences or broad industrial announcements. This page consequently remains an incomplete category account.
